## Round 2026-11-23 browser result cost and scratch cleanup

- Ranked list of what was reachable, most valuable first. 1. The page list that the playwriter launcher appends to every result was repeated on nearly every call (a bug in gm's own launcher patch). 2. gm-tool scratch that a killed run strands. 3. Fixed waitForTimeout sleeps with no early-return hint. 4. Log growth (browser.log, gate.log, run logs). 5. Screenshot size and a page-ready helper (not reachable without changing the upstream playwriter package).
- Evidence for the browser cost (the docstudio session transcript under /config/.claude/projects/-config-docstudio, read only; the docstudio browser and repo were not touched). One session made 109 browser calls: 102 fixed waitForTimeout sleeps adding up to 823 s, 69 screenshots, a median of 16.7 s between calls, and a window of 24 minutes with 84 model turns read 12 million tokens from cache, so each tool result repeated in context is paid on every later turn. 79 of 89 results carried a full page list (1.4 KB each, 108 KB in all, with Gmail addresses of 150 characters). The launcher patch already skipped an unchanged list, but it compared the text including the scan time in the line "browsers: 1 open on this machine (scan 15 ms)", which differs on every call, so the skip never fired.
- Fix 1, defaults/playwriter/launcher-feedback.diff: the comparison strips the scan time (SCAN_TIME_PATTERN). lib/browsers.js caches a scan for 2 s, so a call right after another reuses the same list, and a list changed in the last 2 s shows on the next call.
- Fix 3, defaults/playwriter/launcher-wait-hint.diff: the first call of a launcher process whose code sleeps 5000 ms or more in waitForTimeout gets one text block saying the sleep length and naming page.waitForFunction and locator.waitFor, which return when the page is ready. Short waits and later calls get nothing.
- Installer: gm install reapplies the launcher diffs, without npm ci, when the pinned playwriter is present and only launcher hooks are missing (the two new hooks SCAN_TIME_PATTERN and WAIT_HINT_MS). Before, any missing hook ran npm ci, which replaces node_modules under a running playwriter. Applied for real on this machine: the install printed "launcher patches refreshed in /config/.gmnew/pw, node_modules untouched", the launcher parses (node --check), and the docstudio gate (pid 37204) kept running.
- Checks: check-browser-feedback (real gm serve and browser: a first call lists the pages, a call after 2.5 s with no change does not, a title change lists them again, a 5200 ms sleep carries the hint once and a second one does not, a 300 ms wait never does) fails against a launcher copy whose comparison keeps the scan time, and fails on the hint when the hint is disabled, and passes on the real launcher. check-launcher-refresh (sandbox installs with the offline git and npm stubs: an older launcher is refreshed, the node_modules sentinel survives, no full reinstall) fails with 2 failures when the refresh path is disabled.
- Scratch: gm-tool check roots its TMPDIR at g<pid> and removes it at exit; ship builds Phase B in gm-ship-<sha8>-<pid>, about 2 GB, kept on failure. A run killed by a signal left both for good. gm-tool check and ship now remove the ones that carry gm-tool's marker (.gm-tool-scratch inside g<pid>, a .gm-ship-copy file beside a ship copy) and whose process is gone, and nothing else (native/components/tool/scratch.cpp). check-scratch-sweep runs a real gm-tool check against a fabricated temp directory: dead marked root and ship copy removed; live ones, unmarked ones and other names kept; it fails with 2 failures when the sweep is disabled. A failed ship keeps its copy until the next ship removes it.
- Decided against and measured: pruning run logs (33 runs in docstudio use 5 MB, the largest run is 1.2 MB, and they are the witnesses), capping gate.log (5 KB) and browser.log (230 KB a day, about 85 MB a year, and only while a browser stays up), screenshot downscaling or a page-ready helper (they live in the upstream playwriter package and its executor, so a patch would carry a vendored fork for a saving the model can take itself with the hint), and sweeping /config/tmp entries that gm-tool did not mark (the old gm-* files there belong to earlier lineages).

## Round 2026-11-23 CI margins: Intel macOS job, timer bound, push without a CI wait

- Intel macOS job. Step timings of the last 10 release runs (gh run view, per job): x64-macos total 1119 to 1657 s (18.7 to 27.6 min) and one 30.4 min run cancelled by the 30 minute cap; arm64-macos total 753 to 1117 s. Where the x64 time goes: Test 970 to 1400 s against 690 to 830 s on arm64; Package 80 to 117 s against 4 to 5 s on arm64 and 1 s on Linux; build 25 to 60 s with a warm ccache and 105 to 260 s when a header changes (a cache key problem it is not: both architectures show the same pattern); runner queue 2 to 4 s; the Chromium and playwriter steps 30 to 55 s. The job is slow because macos-latest is Apple silicon and the x64 build runs under Rosetta, and because Phase B ran on one lane: the lane count was floor(cores/2) and a hosted macOS runner has 3 cores. The sum of the checks of the cancelled run was 1268 s of 1332 s wall (jobs 1, load 4.8 on 3 cores), and the longest checks wait on timers (check-restart-jobs 154 s, check-job-wait-bounded 91 s, check-job-status-wait 86 s), so a second lane overlaps waiting.
- Fixes. Lanes are ceil(cores/2) (native/components/tool/driver.cpp; 4-core Linux and Windows runners stay at 2, 3-core macOS goes from 1 to 2; a check that fails in the pool is rerun alone, so contention cannot turn a pass into a red). gm-tool package prints the seconds of each phase and, when sysctl.proc_translated is 1, runs strip and tar through arch -arm64 with a fallback to the plain tools. That translated universal tools are the 90 s in Package is a hypothesis; the printed lines of this push's run settle it. release.yml takes timeout-minutes from matrix.minutes (45 for x64-macos, 30 for the others): 45 minutes is 1.6 times the slowest completed run (27.6 min) and 1.5 times the cancelled one, and the other builds finished within 18.7 minutes, so 30 stays 1.6 times.
- Not measurable on this x64 Linux host: the Rosetta cost, the macOS lane effect and the Package cause. The witness is the x64-macos job of this push (expected Test about 800 s if the lanes overlap the timer waits; read its Package step lines "gm-tool package: ... took").
- check-embedded-runtime. 60 timers of 300 ms on this host gave waited 300 (54 times) and 301 (6 times), and performance.now measured 299.34 to 300.48 ms, so a timer fires up to one tick early on a fine clock. The bound is derived: a libuv timer can fire two loop ticks early (the loop clock lags the real clock by up to a tick and truncates to a tick) and Date.now truncates one more, so the check measures the tick of Date.now in the body and allows three of them (3 ms where the tick is 1 ms). Load only makes timers late, so the bound does not depend on load. 298 ms (the arm64 ASan failure) passes; a timer set to fire at 250 ms fails with waited 250 against at most 3 ms early (checked by mutating the body's delay).
- ship --push. It now returns right after the push: it reads the release and arm-diagnose runs once, with up to 30 s for the runs to appear so their ids are named, and prints green (exit 0), RED (exit 1) or "unconfirmed" with the run ids and the one gh run list command (exit 2). GM_SHIP_CI_WAIT_MINUTES=n waits only when asked; GM_SHIP_CI_POLL_SECONDS and GM_SHIP_CI_ORIGIN_URL are seams for the check. check-ship-push now covers the default return (under 20 s, ids, command), runs that appear late, a red run, and a wait to green; with the default set to one minute it fails ("the default push waited for CI (60 s)"). The dev skill's push line and AGENTS.md say so.
- Decided against: an arm64 build of gm-tool for the Package step (it would add a build to the job), skipping macOS Phase B checks (the platform is what they cover), a cache key change (the build step is not the slow one), and pushing the CI margins separately (one push).

## Round 2026-11-23 gated push, early-return checks, stackuse margin

- Ranked list of what was reachable, most valuable first. 1. A push that cannot go ahead of its project's checks (the docstudio peer pushed 65681e212 before npm run check exited 0 and the Cloud Build gate failed on literals; its owner then asked for a repository script). 2. check-restart-jobs, the longest Phase B check, slept a fixed 150 s. 3. The asan-arm-stackuse job takes 37 to 47 minutes (13 runs) against a 60 minute cap, and its log showed no per-check time. 4. The AGENTS.md note that the skill must stay under 20000 characters was stale. 5. The other long checks (see the decisions below).
- git_push gate (native/components/verbs/git.cpp, verbs.cpp). gm.git_push({ gate: '<command>', gateTimeoutMs }) runs the command in the repository and pushes main only when it exits 0. It refuses before the gate when tracked changes are uncommitted (the gate would check a different tree than the one pushed), refuses when the gate times out or exits non-zero (the reply carries its exit code, seconds and last 1500 characters of output), refuses when the gate changed HEAD or a tracked file, and an empty gate is an error. The reply of a push carries gate with the seconds and the 12 characters of the commit checked. Without gate the verb is unchanged. The one-liner is in the gm skill (20568 characters; check-skill-read-fallback, check-no-resource-client, check-skill-serve and check-skill-reload ok), README.md and the verb's description. check-git covers a red gate (exit 3, output shown, the remote still empty), a dirty tracked tree, a gate that edits a tracked file, an empty gate and a green gate (the remote's main equals HEAD); with the exit-code test disabled it fails ("a gate that exits 3 did not refuse the push").
- AGENTS.md audit: check names, paths and identifiers were checked against the tree (checks.def, git ls, git grep); the only stale note was the skill size one, now corrected (aaafcccc made a whole-text read return the whole skill).
- check-restart-jobs. The carried job was sleep 150; it now waits for a release file the check writes once the restart, the job's process and its running state are proven, so the rest of the check (exit 0, output done, carry-over event, no kill with reason restart) is unchanged. Wall 150 s to 1.1 s; the Phase B wall of 548 s was set by this check and the 90, 85 and 65 s ones. The other long checks were read and kept: check-job-wait-bounded (90 s), check-job-status-wait (85 s) and check-job-wait (65 s) prove that a wait of that length inside one body returns, so the wall time is the property; check-browser-first-open (8 s and 20 s), check-lazy-cache (5 s), check-turn-end-release (2 s), check-browser-blank-grace (7 s), check-browser-idle-default and check-idle-cpu prove that something stays up or stays quiet for a window, which cannot return early; check-update-checked, check-update-checkout and check-relay-reexec already poll and return on the first sighting (1 to 14 s).
- asan-arm-stackuse. 13 runs took 37 to 47 minutes (the check step 2540 s; build 156 s) against a 60 minute cap, 1.28 times the slowest, so the cap is now 80 (1.7 times). gm-tool check now flushes each result and prints "<check>: took N s" on stderr, so the next run's log shows which checks take the 42 minutes; splitting the list over two parallel jobs is the next step once those times are read.
- Witnesses needed in Phase B: gate, check-git, check-restart-jobs, check-scratch-root, check-ship-push; the single push for the whole stretch after the macOS result is read (run 45154367324).

## Round 2026-11-23 the browser's own start failure

- What the CI log held. The failed call of run 45154367324 did carry the browser's reason: the gate answers the websocket upgrade of a failed start with 503 and the reason as its body, and playwright puts that body into the call log of the connectOverCDP error. The check clipped the reply at 240 characters, so the log showed nothing past the gate's port. Measured with a wrapper browser that exits 7 on start after writing 120 noise lines, a path of another project, an API key assignment, a URL with a password and a token query: the unsanitized body reached the reply twice with all of those in it (5 failures of the new check against the first launcher patch).
- Fix (defaults/playwriter/launcher-start-reason.diff, hooks START_REASON_CHARS and the sanitized 503 text). startReason() turns a start failure message into at most 600 characters (200 from the start, 400 from the end): whitespace collapsed, this project's path shortened to <project>/, URLs replaced by <url>, other absolute paths by <path>, KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/AUTH/COOKIE/CREDENTIAL pairs and Bearer values redacted, 32 or more character tokens replaced. The gate sends it as the 503 body of an upgrade or an HTTP request, and records it as lastStartFailure, which its status shows and its header prints as "last browser start failed: ..." while the browser is not running and clears on the next successful start. The message already held the exit status or signal and the last 8 lines of browser.log (browserLogTail); those now survive the clip. The host's path needed no change: the failed call's reply carries the body, and a call that cannot connect is resent five times first (the previous round's fix).
- Check: check-browser-start-reason (real browser, exclusive). A wrapper browser that always exits 7 on start; the failed call's reply must name "last browser start failed", "exited (7)", the last stderr lines, none of the first lines of the noise, none of otherproject, sk-secret-abc123, hunter2, zzz9, qqq, and the start-failure segment stays under 800 characters. With the header and the 503 text replaced by a fixed phrase it fails with 3 failures; with only the first launcher patch (header, raw 503 body) it failed with the 5 leak assertions. A launcher that lacks the hook is refused with a message naming the diff, and gm install refreshes it without npm ci (check-launcher-refresh stays ok).
- release.yml: a failed build job now uploads build/<preset>/phase-b-logs as the artifact phase-b-logs-<target> (5 days). The per-check log holds the whole output of the check, so a red check no longer depends on what its failure text clipped. Windows jobs do not run Phase B and are unchanged.
- AGENTS.md: the browser start-failure narrative moved to docs/MEASURED_FACTS.md, Browser, leaving the rule and a pointer (27376 to 26932 bytes with this round's additions).
- Ranked list sent with this round: 1. the browser's own failure reason (done above); 2. the full output of a red check in CI (artifact, done); 3. AGENTS.md headroom (3.3 KB; one move done, another candidate is the 2043 character Browser note); 4. splitting asan-arm-stackuse over two parallel jobs, which waits for the per-check timings of run 45162429895; 5. widening or removing the other 240 and 300 character clips of replies in checks (check-browser-tabs-owner, check-browser-scope-identity and others), which the artifact makes less urgent.

Reproduced here with a standalone program built with the preset's flags (-O0 -g -fsanitize=address): 5.2 s with the detector on, 3.3 s off, 0.2 s at -O2; with a substring prefilter that skips every line without a "(" and one of Create, spawn, exec, fork, system, popen, Shell, WinExec (every alternative of the regex holds one), 781 lines reach the regex and the same 7 matches come out in 0.3 s. std::regex recurses deeply and the detector instruments every frame, which is why arm64's 555 s is about 100 times the x64 figure; the arm64 time itself is not reproducible here. ### 59. parity-contract: the cause of the intermittent failure, and its fix

- Failure: b16 on 6c8438d, and in the first 4cdbe91 test: "W17/W18: the first gm install --local failed: playwriter clone failed:", empty detail. The run alone passed. The failing spawn was proc::run's rc != 0 return (started false), so the detail was empty; with item 57's wording the same spawn reads "could not start git".
- Cause, in two parts, both in the test's inputs (native/components/tool/checks/parity_contract.cpp runs its witnesses on parallel std::async threads, and support.hpp install_argv gave every install the shared sandbox/offline-bin):
  1. Shared file: install_argv rewrote sandbox/offline-bin/git (and npm, patch-package.js) on every call, from several witness threads at once. A rewrite truncates the file, so an exec of it fails with ETXTBSY. Reproduced on this host with a shell loop that rewrites an executable while another loop runs it: 84 "Text file busy" in 3000 runs.
  2. Inherited write descriptor: write_script used std::ofstream, which opens without close-on-exec. A child that another witness spawned while the stub was open for writing inherits the write descriptor and keeps the file busy until that child exits (for a long-lived gm serve child, that is the whole check). Reproduced in Python with the same fd flags: an inheritable descriptor, child spawned while open, exec of the file fails with errno 26 ETXTBSY; with close-on-exec, exec runs.
- Fix: install_argv writes its offline fixture under its own home (home/offline-bin; the per-witness home is already unique), and the sandbox parameter is removed from install_argv and its eight callers (the parameter had no other use). write_script opens the file with O_CLOEXEC and writes it in POSIX calls, so no child keeps it busy after its exec; under the _WIN32 guard the install path already uses.
- Witness: 10 runs of parity-contract on the rebuilt binary, all RC 0, each "ok (18 of 18 parity contract witnesses hold ...)", none with "could not start" (gate ticket gm-parity-fix2, DONE rc=0). I did not reproduce the failure before the fix on demand; the mechanism and its fix are the evidence, and the 10 runs show it stable.
- Not ours, seen in the build: browser_start_reason.cpp:36 "lines_in defined but not used" (origin commit). Left as is.

The recorded seconds are now the measured ones: shard 1 964.6 s, shard 2 936.7 s (3 percent apart; they were 964 and 946). check-asan-shards passes with them (timeout 35 minutes against 33 needed at 1.6 times setup plus the slowest shard). What it still does under the detector at -O0 is walk 239 files, read 41026 lines into vectors of strings and run the substring prefilter on each; the regex now runs on 781 of them. It is no longer on the critical path (shard 2 ends 22 s before shard 1 whichever way it moves), so nothing was changed.
- Fixed timers that remain (survey of sleep_for, wait_for and sleep in native/ and the checks): the product has none above 250 ms that cannot be woken (relay settle 250 ms, kill grace 500 ms, a 5 s wait_for on a download that returns when it finishes, progress ticks scaled by clock_scale). In the checks, every dwell above a few seconds asserts that something does NOT happen, and its length is the product's own constant: check-browser-first-open 8 s (GRACE_MS 5 s plus a tick) and 20 s (PLAYWRITER_IDLE_MS 20000), check-browser-blank-grace 7 s (BLANK_GRACE_MS 20 s), check-lazy-cache 5 s, check-turn-end-release 2 s. A shorter dwell would pass a gate that closes the tab later than the constant says, so they stay. The longest waits (check-job-wait-bounded 90 s, check-job-status-wait 84 s, check-job-wait 65 s) measure a real wait against the 60 s next_context cap and the 100 s foreground cap that sits under the client's 120 s, so scaling them with GM_CLOCK_SCALE would stop witnessing the one thing they exist for; decided against.
- Found instead: Phase B on the tar copy ordered its checks by a flat 30 s each. The driver sorts its pool longest first from build/release/phase-b-durations.txt, and a ship copy starts with no such file, so the 60 to 90 s checks started wherever the registration order put them. Also the file recorded the wall of failed checks: the one in the checkout held 60.3 s for check-update-checked and check-update-checkout, which were the timeouts of a run in a dirty checkout (their logs say no update cycle was logged within 60 s), and 150 s for check-restart-jobs, which is a sleep that was removed. Fix: ship copies the checkout's file into the copy before Phase B and copies the copy's back after a pass; the driver records the wall of a passing check only. The stale file in the checkout was deleted. check-ship-push has a scenario for both copies (fails with two failures when either is removed). The ordering gain was not measured; it needs one more ship to see the "longest:" line against the 461.7 s of the last copy run (143 checks).
- Witnesses needed in Phase B: gate, check-ship-push, check-asan-shards; in the next arm-diagnose run the same per-check seconds again if the numbers are to be trusted beyond one run.
- Found and fixed while reading the gate for the handoff question: a second gate for the same project stopped the first gate's browser. Reproduced here with the installed launcher in a scratch project: node playwriter-project start (gate 1499147, browser 1499169), then node playwriter-project --gate on the same ports. The second gate failed with EADDRINUSE, and its listen-failure handler called exitGate with force, which called releaseBrowser; the gate had no browser of its own, but stopChrome treats the pid in the profile's SingletonLock as owned, so the log reads "stopping browser: gate listen failed on 9422: listen EADDRINUSE" and "browser stopped" and the first gate's Chrome (with its tabs) was gone. A real start does this whenever two launchers find no gate in the same few seconds (two peers calling together after a gate ended, or the handoff below). Fix: defaults/playwriter/launcher-listen-failure.diff (exitGate takes keepBrowser, the listen-failure handler passes it); hook "launcher keeps the first gate's browser when its port is taken" (keepBrowser: true) and its mirror in the offline fake git; check-browser-second-gate (real browser, exclusive): start, then a second --gate, then the browser pid with the same start time and the first gate must be alive. It passes installed, and fails with the one guard line removed from the installed launcher (the gate log shows the stop), restored after. The chain of five diffs applies on the pinned base in order and equals the installed file.
- Proposal, not done: how the long-running docstudio gate (pid 37204, up two days, launcher of 22 November) could pick up the new launcher without closing the browser and its signed-in tabs. Read without touching it: the gate is ppid 1 in its own session; its Chrome (pid 37235) is its own process group and session, child of the gate only by parentage, with stdout and stderr on the project's browser.log, so no pipe ties them.
  - What does not work: SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP to the gate. Its handler is exitGate with force, which stops a browser the gate started (Browser.close, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 and 5 s); that closes the tabs, and the profile on disk keeps the logins but not the open pages. Also not a restart through a launcher call: replaceStaleGate signals the gate the same way when the browser fingerprint differs.
  - What would work: SIGKILL to the gate pid, by pid and start time. The gate dies at once and Chrome stays up, re-parented to init; browser.pid, browser.fingerprint and the profile lock stay on disk. The next call of any peer runs ensureGate, which starts a gate from the launcher file on disk (the new one) on the same gate port (the state file keeps it) and the same debug port (Chrome's). On the first browser request the new gate finds the debug port answering and calls adopt: the listener pid equals the recorded pid, so it takes the browser as its own (not the ADOPTED warning) and keeps it, provided the fingerprint matches.
  - Risks, most serious first. (1) The fingerprint is computed from the environment of the process that spawns the new gate (PLAYWRITER_BROWSER_PATH, PLAYWRITER_NO_SANDBOX, PLAYWRITER_WEBGPU), and ensureGate passes the caller's environment; if it differs from the old gate's, adopt sees a changed fingerprint and stops and restarts Chrome, which is the thing to avoid. Compare those three variables of /proc/37204/environ with the peer's before, and do not run it from a shell whose environment differs. (2) Two launchers racing to start the new gate: before the listen-failure fix above the loser stopped the browser; with it the loser exits and leaves it. The fix has to be in the installed launcher before the SIGKILL, and a new gate started after it carries it. (3) Every websocket through the gate drops: the executor's connection dies, so a body running at that moment fails, a context made with browser.newContext() is disposed, and the executor's state object is lost; pages in the default context (the signed-in tabs) survive. The host resends a call that fails before its body runs, up to five times. Do it between calls, when status shows no call in flight. (4) The new gate has the blank-tab sweep (20 s grace) active for the first time: a tab that sits on about:blank for 20 s is closed. (5) The gate's in-memory lease table and hold time are lost; leases come back with the peers' next call. (6) Without the old gate there is a gap of about 1 s; a call in it takes the ensureGate path (5 s allowed).
  - Witness first, in a scratch project, before anyone touches the real one: start gate and browser with the old launcher (the file from the pinned base plus the four diffs of 22 November), SIGKILL the gate, make one call with the new launcher, and read that the browser pid and its start time are unchanged, an open page and a cookie are still there, and the new gate reports the browser as its own. That is a check worth adding (check-gate-handoff) and was not written in this round.
  - Forward fix so the next upgrade needs no SIGKILL: a SIGUSR2 handler that exits the gate without releasing the browser (dropSockets, keep browser.pid and the fingerprint), and a launcher build id in /__pwp/ping so a launcher call that sees a gate older than its own file asks for that exit while no lease is held. It cannot reach the gate that runs today, which has no such handler.
- Witnesses needed in Phase B: gate, check-browser-second-gate, check-launcher-refresh, check-ship-push, check-asan-shards.

## Round 2026-11-24 the forward fix for the gate handoff, rehearsed in a scratch project

- Done as proposed, not applied to the docstudio gate (pid 37204 and its browser 37235 were not touched; the check scans their processes read-only and its start time is unchanged). defaults/playwriter/launcher-ws-handoff.diff (applied last in sorted order; the seven diffs in order give the same file as the edited one): the launcher computes LAUNCHER_BUILD, the first 12 hex of the sha256 of its own file; /__pwp/ping carries it; GET /__pwp/handoff answers 409 with the lease count while any lease is held, otherwise answers ok and the gate exits through exitGate with keepBrowser (the browser, browser.pid and the fingerprint stay); ensureGate, when the gate's build differs from its own, calls the handoff, waits up to 15 s for the ping to stop and then starts a gate from its own file, which adopts the running browser; SIGUSR2 (not on Windows) does the same for an operator. A gate without a build in its ping (the 22 November one) is left alone. Hook "launcher hands an idle gate over to a newer launcher build" in install.cpp and its needle in the offline fake git.
- Risk of the design, not removed: two live launchers of different builds could hand a gate back and forth, but only while it holds no lease, and a proxy holds a lease for its whole connection, so a gate in use is never handed over; an idle one is replaced at most once per caller. The handoff route is a GET on the loopback port like /__pwp/hold, so a web page could ask an idle gate to restart; the browser and its tabs survive that, the gate's websockets drop.
- check-gate-handoff (browser_launcher_gate.cpp), scratch project only: one browser outlived five gates. (1) A launcher copy of a newer build runs start: the idle gate is handed over and the new gate runs the same browser (same pid and start time). (2) kill -USR2 ends that gate and not the browser; a launcher started afterwards adopts it. (3) The 22 November launcher, composed in the check from the pinned base plus launcher-feedback.diff and launcher-wait-hint.diff (no blank-tab sweep, no sanitized start text), starts a gate that adopts the same browser. (4) SIGKILL of that old gate by pid leaves the browser up. (5) A current launcher then starts a gate that adopts it, and the gate log says "adopted running browser". Passes (4.5 s); with the automatic handoff disabled in the installed launcher it fails with two named lines (the previous gate still running, no new gate took over); the launcher was restored byte for byte. The scenario 3 to 5 rehearsal is the one for the real gate: same environment for the old and new launcher, so the fingerprint matched; with another PLAYWRITER_BROWSER_PATH or NO_SANDBOX the new gate would stop the browser and start its own, as the earlier proposal says.
- What remains for the docstudio gate: it still runs the old launcher and has no handoff route or signal handler. SIGKILL by pid and start time is the only way, when the owner decides; the rehearsal shows the browser survives it and the next launcher adopts it. Not done.
- Witnesses needed in Phase B: gate, check-gate-handoff, check-browser-ws-address, check-launcher-refresh.

## Round 2026-11-25 release 45352460715 red on one job: arm64 macOS, check-browser-first-open

- Run: release 45352460715 (bad72922, the gate handoff) failed only on build (macos-latest, arm64-macos-release); arm-diagnose 45352460730 and the other seven build jobs passed. Release 45349619832 (20e21e51) was green on every platform.
- Failed check: check-browser-first-open, 43.2 s, two failures in the gate-loss step: the status read after the second open found "gate": null (gate pid 0), so no SIGKILL was sent, and the call after it found a gate (pid 91044, one lease, a fresh browser) whose page list was only about:blank, so the page the check had just opened was not there. check-gate-handoff, check-browser-ws-address, check-browser-second-gate and the other browser checks passed on that job (phase-b-logs-arm64-macos).
- Not caused by the handoff as far as shown: the same job shape ran check-browser-first-open with the handoff launcher in 20 further macOS jobs (arm64 and x64, runs 45506648634 to 45531647283, ten commits by another agent on top of bad72922) and it passed in all 20; and 9 runs here under 6 busy loops and 3 parallel instances all passed (73 to 88 s). The handoff route answers only a caller whose launcher build differs from the gate's, and every process in this check runs one launcher file.
- Cause not established: the check read the gate once, with a 2 s ping inside `status`, and never read the second open's reply, so the log cannot tell a gate that was not up from a ping that timed out, nor an open that failed from one that landed on a gate that then exited. The gate exits 0 to 5 s after its browser is down (tick, 5 s) and this check starts its second session right after the browser's debug port closes, so the second open can meet a gate on its way out; that is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
- Change (native/components/tool/checks/browser_first_open.cpp): the second open's reply is checked (a failure shows the executor's error), the gate is polled for up to 20 s instead of read once, and any failure in that step appends the tails of gate.log and browser.log. Shown here: with PLAYWRITER_BROWSER_PATH=/bin/false the check now reports "the second open did not show a crossOriginIsolated page: browserType.connectOverCDP ... 503" plus the gate log tail ("browser start failed: browser exited (1) ..."); the old check showed neither in that step. A healthy run passes (44.0 s).
- Done condition: the next macOS failure of this check, if any, names whether the open failed and what the gate log says; a run with no failure leaves the cause open.
- Seen on origin while reading logs, not touched: check-cut-marker and check-retry-hints fail on all four non-Windows build jobs of runs 45523170450, 45526267962, 45530440385 and 45531647283 (another agent's commits 068845fc to dccfdf1f).

## Round 2026-11-25 docstudio's project browser was stopped by a lease gap: cause, fix, cookies

- Windows saving from the release run after the clean host rebuild went (45601313491 against 45610111005): x64 job 1134 s to 620 s (Configure and build 567 s to 588 s, Clean host rebuild 541 s to none), arm64 job 986 s to 535 s (423 s to 424 s, 383 s to none). 514 s and 451 s saved, 45 and 46 percent; Worker binary versions passed its new version assertion on both.
- What the log shows (/config/docstudio/.playwriter/gate.log, read only): on 2026-11-23 the gate adopted pid 37235 (10:57) and kept it through many "probe failed 1/3: timeout after 3000 ms" lines (the browser, busy with its tabs, often did not answer in 3 s) and many "last lease released" lines that each ended in "no lease, but a start hold or an open page keeps the browser up". On 2026-11-25 10:16:26 the last lease was released; 8 s later (grace 5 s) the same path logged "stopping browser: no lease for the grace period", with "probe failed 1/3: timeout after 3000 ms" one second after it, and the browser stopped at 10:16:38.
- Cause: the launcher's isHeld (the grace-stop and tick path, in the 22 November launcher the gate ran and in every later one) began with "if the browser does not answer /json/version, it is not held" and read a timed-out /json/list as "no open page". A browser that was alive with 8 tabs but did not answer within 3 s at that moment was therefore treated as having no pages, and exitUnleased stopped it. Not the idle stop (idle was 8 h), not the adoption path (10:57 on the 23rd only adopted it), and not the handoff or the other diffs of the last days: the gate that stopped it ran code from 22 November (no handoff route, no ws-address diff); the same grace path had stopped docstudio browsers on 2026-11-20 at 09:31 and 15:00.
- After the stop (10:17:56 to 10:27): five more gates started browsers (pids 2324136 to 2341515); the first was stopped normally (no pages), and the next four each lost their browser 30 to 170 s after it started with "probe failed 1/3: connection error ECONNREFUSED" and no "stopping browser" line, then exited "no lease for the grace period". The gate did not stop them, and gate.log and browser.log hold no crash or signal line; what ended those browsers is not established. The browser now running (2341515, started 10:27:06) is the last of them.
- Fix: defaults/playwriter/launcher-zz-keep-pages.diff: isHeld answers "held" when the browser does not answer but its process lives (browserDead() is false), and only a dead browser, or an answered /json/list without a caller page and no start hold, releases it. Stopped by idle, an explicit close, or a dead process, never by a lease gap with pages open.
- Check: check-browser-keeps-pages starts a gate, opens a page, waits for the gate to see it, stops the browser's process with SIGSTOP for 20 s (the grace period passes), resumes it and asserts the same browser pid and its page are still there; a second case with PLAYWRITER_IDLE_MS=8000 asserts the idle timeout still stops a browser with an open page. Red before the diff: "stopping browser: no lease and no open page" after two "probe failed" lines, browser gone; green after.
- Cookies (measured here, Chromium /usr/bin/chromium, the binary docstudio runs, graceful Browser.close then start, headless): a persistent cookie survives; a session cookie (no expiry) does not, and the tabs are not reopened. With --restore-last-session (or Preferences session.restore_on_startup 1, same effect) the session cookie and the tabs survive. A Google sign-in held in session cookies, or in cookies Chrome treats as session, is lost on any stop without it. Change: defaults/playwriter/launcher-zzz-restore-session.diff adds the flag when PLAYWRITER_RESTORE_SESSION=1 and defaults/mcp.json sets it in envDefaults (a layer that restates the whole entry replaces it). Check: check-browser-session-restore (1: persistent,sess survive; 0: only persistent). Consequence: after a stop the next browser reopens the tabs of the last session, which are not owned by any run (browser_tabs counts them as other runs').
- Not changed: a browser killed with SIGKILL (not stopped) can lose cookies Chrome had not flushed (about 30 s); the docstudio gate and Chrome were not touched, so its running gate still has the old isHeld until it is replaced (handoff proposal, 2026-11-24 round) and its profile is not restored automatically.

### check-browser-feedback failed once in Phase B of e71e593c (not the keep-pages change)

- Phase B on the copy: 162 run, 1 failed: check-browser-feedback, "a call after which no page changed repeated the page list" (log kept by the new failed-ship path at build/release/phase-b-logs-failed). The same failure then appeared 1 in 12 under load with PLAYWRITER_RESTORE_SESSION=0 (so not the restore flag), and in 13 of 24 runs with six checks in parallel.
- Cause, read from the repeated list once the check printed it: the page list the launcher puts after a call is machine-wide (every Chromium on the host), so a change in another browser between two calls (another check's browser, or docstudio's running browser, whose window count is 3) repeats it. This host runs the real docstudio browser, so Phase B here is exposed to it; CI runners are not. The launcher is right to repeat a changed list.
- Change (native/components/tool/checks/browser_feedback.cpp): the no-repeat assertion takes up to three consecutive calls and fails only when all three repeat or lose the gate line, and its failure now prints the repeated list from the return value on. A launcher that always repeated would still fail all three. One more failure seen under load was the first call timing out at 10 s ("Code execution timed out"), which is load and unrelated.
### 73. read_file cap by unit: one 12000-character cap for lines and chars, so a page is never cut in band (Phase A, not run)

- Held item 5 (the cap by unit), decided here under the owner's maximal-scope rule. Two caps stood on one reply: the verb packed a line page to 20000 characters and a chars page to a limit of 20000, while the in-band cut (server.cpp bounded_output) cut at 12000. A page of 12000 to 20000 characters was therefore cut, and its hint asked the reader to switch unit to chars, which worked around the mismatch instead of removing it.
- Decision: one cap, 12000 characters, named gm::marker::kInlineChars (native/include/gm/marker.hpp). The verb sizes every read_file page to it through read_page (native/components/verbs/core_internal.hpp): a line page packs whole lines while they fit, and a chars page clamps its limit to 12000. A read_file page is therefore never cut in band; the unit only says how the range is counted. The lines-page and over-cap hints are removed from bounded_output (native/components/mcp/server.cpp); the whole-read hint stays.
- Breaking change, pre-alpha, recorded in the REPORT: a lines read may return fewer lines than its limit, with nextOffset at the first line not returned; a chars read with a limit above 12000 returns 12000 characters and nextOffset 12000. The limit error text, read_file's description and the served skill say so; the run_code cut threshold named in the skill and in docs/PARITY_CONTRACT.md is 12000 (it said 6000, which was stale since 068845f).
- Check: check-read-range-clamp (native/components/tool/checks/read_range_clamp.cpp): a chars read of limit 20000 over a 30000-character file returns 12000 characters, nextOffset 12000, and a hint with offset: 12000. check-read-lines-pack (native/components/tool/checks/read_lines_pack.cpp): 60 lines of 300 characters read with offset 0 and limit 60 returns a page of 11000 to 12000 characters (38 lines, 11733 characters) that is not cut in band, with nextOffset equal to its line count and a hint with that offset. check-read-parity (read_parity.cpp): the probe table now states the 12000 page, the clamp probe, and the cut-line hint at offset 12025.

## Round 2026-11-26 the two ARM Linux reds of edd6abed (releases 45630182177 and 45630183268)

- Read from the logs (gh run view --log, and the phase-b-logs-arm64-linux artifact): build (ubuntu-24.04-arm) failed on check-browser-session-restore, "with PLAYWRITER_RESTORE_SESSION=0 the cookies after a stop and start were [], expected [persistent]" (the check took 8.7 s there against 15 to 25 s here); asan-arm-stackuse (1) stopped on check-restart-jobs with "basic_filebuf::underflow error reading the file: No such process" and exit code 2 and no FAILED line, because the exception left gm-tool.
- check-browser-session-restore (my check of e71e593c) is the first cause and the fault is its timing: after Browser.close it slept a fixed 1 s and then ran start. A browser that is still closing answers the probe, so start returned a dying browser and the read script's websocket closed with no reply (empty output on the runner, ECONNREFUSED or HTTP 503 here). Red before: with the sleep at 0, 3 of 6 parallel runs failed here (ECONNREFUSED twice, start reporting HTTP 503 once). Green after: the check waits for the old browser's pid and start time to change (60 s ceiling) before start, 8 parallel runs passed 7 and the eighth hit the scratch race below, then 1 of 1 clean. The product behaviour it exposed, start returning a browser that is closing, is not changed here; it may be the cause of the four browsers of the 25 November docstudio log that died with ECONNREFUSED right after their start (not proven).
- check-restart-jobs is the second cause and it is not a new check: proc::start_time_of, proc::command_of and the environ reads went through std::istreambuf_iterator over /proc/<pid>/..., and a read after the process was reaped fails with ESRCH, which libstdc++ throws out of the iterator as basic_filebuf::underflow. A scratch program of the same pattern threw 1109 times in 2.1 million reads here. check-proc-read-exits (new) spawns short children and reads them until they are gone: 194 exceptions before, none after (692 children, 266939 reads). Fix: proc::read_text_of (fopen and fread, a failed read ends the text) at every /proc read that used the iterator: proc.cpp (stat, cmdline), driver.cpp and checks (environ, stat). This also removes a crash path of the gm worker itself (reap_ledger and the process scans call these).
- A third fault, found while proving the first: gm-tool check removed a live gm-tool check's scratch root. sweep_dead_scratch took the process table first and listed the temp directory second, so a root created between the two (a check process that started in between) named a pid that was not in the table and was swept ("filesystem error: temp_directory_path: No such file or directory" in 1 of 8 parallel runs here). The sweep now lists first and takes the table after. check-scratch-sweep gains a case whose process table call creates a marked root of a live pid: red with the old order (reproduced by swapping the two blocks), green now.
- Not run here: Linux arm64 and the ASan job (no such host). check-proc-read-exits is the load-independent witness of the asan fault; the asan job must show check-restart-jobs ok.

### Phase A, not pushed: a start reports ready for a browser that is closing (check-browser-start-closing)

- Red first, on the launcher as installed (scratch home with the applied launcher, not ~/.gmnew): `HOME=<home> gm-tool check <gm> check-browser-start-closing` fails with "the browser started after a closing one does not answer the debug port". The start had printed "browser ready" while Chromium was exiting; the gate log had no start line, because the gate's chromeUp was still true.
- The mechanism, measured here with /usr/bin/chromium (headless, node probe): after Browser.close the debug port stops answering about 45 to 70 ms later, the profile's SingletonLock is removed at the same moment, and the process exits about 50 ms after that. So the lock is gone while the process is alive, and a start in that window launched a second browser on the profile; a start while the port still answers was adopted as ready.
- The check stops the browser with SIGSTOP right after it sends Browser.close (so the lock is still there and the port does not answer), resumes it after 3 s from a thread, and runs the CLI start while it is stopped. Assertions: start reports ready, and the debug port answers afterwards.
- Earlier red seen on this host with the close followed by a 0 s start: "browser failed: HTTP 503" after 30 s, the "profile is held by live pid" branch (start deferred, then waitFor(probe) that never answers). That is the path the arm64 run of 45630182177 also reports as a cookie read that found nothing.
- Fix, launcher-zz-start-closing.diff (applied after launcher-zz-keep-pages.diff, before launcher-zzz-restore-session.diff; verified by rebuilding the launcher from the pinned base in that order): (1) startChrome waits up to 30 s until the profile owner is gone or the debug port answers, instead of waiting for the port alone; (2) the CLI start asks the gate for /json/version, and when it answers waits SETTLE_MS (2 s) and asks again; a browser that stopped in between makes the gate restart it on the next ask (START_ATTEMPTS 3). The settle constant is a chosen value: a Chromium close here finishes within 0.1 s, and 2 s covers a slower host; it is not measured on arm64.
- Green after: check-browser-start-closing ok (12.6 s). The same scratch launcher also passed check-browser-session-restore, check-browser-keeps-pages, check-browser-feedback, check-browser-second-gate, check-gate-handoff and check-launcher-refresh (after gm_skills was built).
- Cost: a start that finds the browser running takes 2 s longer (the settle). Calls that do not start a browser are unchanged.
- Not proven: the four browsers of the 25 November docstudio log that died with ECONNREFUSED 30 to 170 s after their start. A close by an external Browser.close, as a body's browser.close() on connectOverCDP would send, is the same mechanism, but the gate's own stop is not affected.
- Install hook: "launcher starts a browser only after a closing one has exited, and reports ready only for one that stays up" (START_ATTEMPTS) and the same needle in the fake git of checks/support.hpp.

### Browser fingerprint mismatch stopped a running browser (check-browser-fingerprint-mismatch, Phase A, not pushed)

- Question (owner): does a fingerprint mismatch stop a browser with pages? Proof from the logs and the code.
- Logs: docstudio gate.log "stopping browser: signal SIGTERM" at 12:44:23, 12:44:38 and 12:45:06 are not a replaceStaleGate SIGTERM. Each follows a scratch experiment of mine: the scratch run's end-of-scenario `kill` ended the gate that the status output had listed first, because the status output lists every browser on the machine and the match took docstudio's gate pid. That kill also sent SIGKILL to docstudio's browser (pid 3133065). This was my mistake: the kill rule is a recorded pid and start time, and the match was not one. No gate or browser is affected by the fix below; the experiment is not repeated.
- Code, which does stop a running browser on a mismatch: (1) replaceStaleGate, run by the CLI start, sends SIGTERM to the project's gate when the recorded fingerprint differs and the gate has no lease; the gate's exit stops its browser (stopChrome) even with pages open. (2) adopt(true) in ensureChrome stops an adopted browser when the fingerprint differs and restarts it. The fingerprint was PLAYWRITER_BROWSER_PATH from the caller's environment or LINUX_BROWSERS, so a caller that lacks the variable computed another value from the gate (docstudio's gate runs with "||").
- Red first: check-browser-fingerprint-mismatch, installed launcher: "replaced the gate (pid N) that held a browser with a page", "stopped by a start whose browser fingerprint differed", "stopped the adopted browser ... that had a page" (SIGUSR2 hands the gate over with its browser, a start from a caller without NO_SANDBOX then adopts). 5 failures.
- Change: defaults/playwriter/launcher-zzzz-fingerprint.diff (applied last; verified by rebuilding the launcher in sorted order). The fingerprint is the realpath of the browser the launcher would launch (PLAYWRITER_BROWSER_PATH, else the first LINUX_BROWSERS entry, else chromium on PATH) plus the flags; a mismatch is logged (fingerprintNote in the CLI start, adopt) and never stops anything. The restart branch and stopAdopted and isOwnGate are removed.
- Green: check-browser-fingerprint-mismatch ok (13.5 s) on the fixed launcher in a scratch home. Also green in the same scratch home: check-browser-start-closing, check-browser-log-bounds, check-browser-keeps-pages, check-browser-second-gate, check-launcher-refresh (hook fingerprintNote), check-browser-feedback. check-browser-session-restore passed 4 of 4 when run alone on both launchers; in one batch with the other checks it failed once ("still running 60 s after Browser.close"), a load flake that is not reproduced alone.
- Known after install: the recorded fingerprint in browser.fingerprint is the old value ("||") until a browser starts again, so the next start logs a note. The docstudio gate (build 1fba5c6e0501) still has the old code until its handover; the first docstudio call from a caller on the new launcher hands it over with its browser kept (the handover path of check-gate-handoff).

### What ended the owner's browser on 26 November (check-browser-last-window, Phase A, not pushed)

- Measured here on a private Xvfb (:99) with a headful /usr/bin/chromium started by the launcher: the client actions page.close() on its own page (with another page open), context.close() on a newContext, context.close() on the default context, and browser.close() on a connectOverCDP browser all left the browser up. Playwright's close on a CDP-connected browser only drops the connection (browserProcess.close is the transport close, not Browser.close).
- Closing every page in the default context, including the last one, ended the browser at once. The gate logged only "last lease released", then "probe failed ECONNREFUSED", then "no lease for the grace period", with no stop line: the signature of 25 November and of 12:05:53. A headful Chromium exits when its last window closes. Adding --keep-alive-for-test did not stop that exit.
- Not proven for the owner's 12:05:53 death: the owner's Chrome was headful on :1 and its tabs at that moment are not known; a last-page close is the mechanism that matches the logs.
- Fix (defaults/playwriter/launcher-zzzzz-anchor.diff): keepAnchor keeps one about:blank page that the gate does not close (its id is the anchor), creates one with PUT /json/new when no blank page exists, runs on every blank sweep and right after each start. The blank-tab sweep skips the anchor. A client's close of its own pages therefore never leaves zero windows. A client that closes every page it can list, the anchor included, still exits the browser; the gate recreates the anchor on its next tick (5 s) after that.
- Red: installed launcher, "closing a client's own page, the last one in the project browser, stopped the browser". Green: the anchor launcher, same check 8.9 s. Also green on the anchor launcher: check-browser-blank-grace, tabs-owner, feedback, keeps-pages, first-open, fingerprint-mismatch, start-closing, session-restore, second-gate, log-bounds, idle-default, gate-handoff.
- Check method notes: the first version of the check closed the gate's blank page as the only window (that is itself a client closing every window, so the browser exited regardless of the fix). Closing /json/close is asynchronous, so a page still listed after close is not yet gone; the check waits for a blank page that is not one it closed. check-browser-last-window runs only when DISPLAY is set; a headless browser does not exit on its last window.
- The earlier "SIGTERM" lines in docstudio's gate.log at 12:44 came from my scratch cleanup (see the fingerprint entry above), not from the launcher.

### Item 2 of the queue: an idle lease blocked every handover; a handover from an older caller replaced a newer gate (check-browser-idle-handover)

- Owner's gate 3163952 (build 1fba5c6e0501) was held by lease pid 2983204 (busy 0, started 08:25, idle for hours). The old handoff route answers 409 whenever any lease is held, so the new launcher could never replace that gate while the idle proxy stayed up.
- Second hazard found while designing it: pid 2983204 runs an older launcher, which hands over any gate whose build differs from its own (ensureGate). Once a handover is allowed, that proxy's next call would replace the newer gate with its older launcher's gate. The rule therefore also refuses a handoff from a caller that is not newer.
- Rule (launcher-zzzzzz-idle-handover.diff): the gate records a lease's last call (lastCall, set on each busy change). A handoff is refused when a lease has busy > 0 or was called within PLAYWRITER_HANDOVER_IDLE_MS (default 60000). A handoff carries loaded=<the caller's launcher file mtime at load>; the gate refuses unless that is newer than its own (old callers send none, so they are refused). ensureGate sends the parameter.
- Red on the installed launcher: "a lease with no call for 4 s (bound 2 s) blocked the handover: status 409" and "a handoff from a caller that is not newer than the gate was accepted: status 200". The busy case passes on both (409 is the control).
- Green on the new launcher (scratch home): check-browser-idle-handover ok (20.9 s, 3 cases), with check-gate-handoff, check-browser-keeps-pages, check-browser-second-gate, check-browser-fingerprint-mismatch, check-browser-last-window and check-browser-log-bounds all ok.
- Limits: the rule runs only in a gate built with it. The owner's running gate (1fba) has the old handoff, so the rule reaches it only when a caller on the new install hands it over while no lease is held. Nothing here stops pid 2983204 or the owner's browser. When the handover does happen, the proxy loses its lease and retires its child process, so its executor state is lost; the browser's pages and sign-in are kept.
